description: Add private, on-demand Bitcoin wallet verification to the web app by comparing ledger balances against balances derived from descriptor-backed Bitcoin accounts over a local Electrum-compatible server, while keeping sensitive descriptor material out of the normal accounting data model by default.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed after Feature-22 establishes Bitcoin node presence on the dashboard and after the team resolves the descriptor parsing and Sparrow wallet-file strategy documented in this PRD.

principles: Descriptor First - multisig and modern wallet setups require full descriptor coverage rather than xpub-only shortcuts
Private by Default - verification secrets are handled ephemerally unless the operator explicitly opts into persistence
Electrum as Common Ground - verification depends on the Electrum protocol, not on any one server implementation
Results Persist, Secrets Usually Do Not - verification outcomes belong in the app's durable record; descriptors usually do not
Sparrow-Aware Operator Workflow - advanced self-custody users should feel like the feature was designed for their tools and threat model
Narrow Claims, High Trust - the feature should state exactly what was verified and avoid overstating coverage

techStack.backendFramework: FastAPI web service with isolated verification service adapters
techStack.frontend: Existing responsive web shell with dashboard and wallet detail surfaces
techStack.testing: pytest API/service tests + targeted frontend smoke coverage
techStack.coreDependencies: Electrum-compatible JSON-RPC server + existing wallet/balance query services + descriptor parsing/derivation layer

userStories.title: Verification domain model and result persistence
acceptanceCriteria: Add a dedicated verification data model separate from normal wallet metadata so verification state does not get mixed into the accounting schema haphazardly
Persist non-sensitive verification outputs such as ledger balance, verified chain balance, drift, height, timestamp, status, and operator-facing error text
Model support for multiple chain accounts per wallet even if the first UI exposes only one verification target
Keep the model compatible with future integrity findings, attestation exports, and alerting
userStories.testStrategy: pytest model and persistence tests on SQLite and PostgreSQL-backed fixtures

userStories.title: Electrum-compatible chain query backend abstraction
acceptanceCriteria: Create a chain-query interface that targets the Electrum protocol rather than a single deployment such as electrs, mempool/electrs, or Frigate
Support the minimum RPC set required for verification including version negotiation, header/tip awareness, balance lookup, history lookup, and optionally UTXO lookup
Handle unreachable, incompatible, or partially degraded servers with operator-readable failure states
Keep the abstraction narrow enough that alternate backends such as Esplora or bitcoind scan RPC could be added later without rewriting verification semantics
userStories.testStrategy: pytest unit tests with mocked Electrum JSON-RPC responses plus protocol compatibility fixtures

userStories.title: Manual descriptor verification session
acceptanceCriteria: Allow an operator to provide descriptor input on demand for a verification session without requiring persistence
Support descriptor sets sufficient for common single-sig and multisig wallet layouts, including external and change branches when applicable
Derive verification targets for a bounded scan window and compare computed chain balance to the ledger balance for the mapped wallet
Discard session-provided descriptor material after verification completes or fails
userStories.testStrategy: pytest verification-service tests with known descriptor fixtures and synthetic Electrum responses

userStories.title: Wallet detail and dashboard verification surfaces
acceptanceCriteria: Expose verified balance, ledger balance, drift, verification status, and last checked time on wallet-facing web surfaces
Clearly distinguish unverified, verified, stale, failed, and partially configured states
Avoid language that implies complete wallet proof when only a registered descriptor account has been checked
Keep the UI useful on mobile while allowing richer drill-down on desktop
userStories.testStrategy: frontend smoke coverage and API payload tests for all verification states

userStories.title: Optional remembered verification sources
acceptanceCriteria: Allow operators to opt into storing a remembered verification source such as descriptor material or a local Sparrow wallet reference
Make the default posture session-only, with clear consent when persistence is enabled
Persist enough metadata to detect an obvious mismatch with a previously verified wallet target, such as a stable wallet fingerprint or descriptor checksum
Keep persisted verification-source data isolated from routine wallet CRUD and tax workflows
userStories.testStrategy: pytest persistence/permission tests and negative tests for mismatched descriptors

userStories.title: Sparrow-aware source integration path
acceptanceCriteria: Document and, if feasible, implement a path for using Sparrow wallet files as an on-demand verification source while preserving Sparrow's encryption posture
Keep Sparrow integration optional so descriptor-based verification can ship even if wallet-file unlock support is deferred
Avoid claiming support for Sparrow wallet-file decryption until the file format and safe unlock flow are verified from primary source code or docs
Preserve a clean abstraction so other descriptor-capable wallet sources can be added later
userStories.testStrategy: research spike + targeted integration tests if wallet-file support is implemented

userStories.title: Integrity findings and alert integration
acceptanceCriteria: Turn meaningful verification mismatches into explicit integrity findings rather than ad hoc UI warnings
Support operator-facing statuses such as new, acknowledged, and resolved where appropriate
Expose enough structured metadata for future attestation or alert exports
Keep routine balance verification useful even before full alerting automation is configured
userStories.testStrategy: pytest finding-generation tests with clean, drifted, and failed verification scenarios

high: Persisting descriptor material incautiously would create a serious privacy and operator-trust failure
If the app overstates what was verified, users may assume a false level of treasury assurance
medium: Descriptor parsing and derivation may prove awkward in pure Python compared with the stronger Rust ecosystem
Electrum-compatible servers can differ at the edges in behavior, performance, and supported protocol versions
Sparrow wallet-file support may require a deeper source-level compatibility effort than is appropriate for the first iteration
low: The core comparison concept is straightforward once descriptors can be derived into scriptPubKeys and queried over Electrum
The feature is naturally opt-in and can remain non-blocking for operators who prefer pure ledger accounting

preFlightChecklist: Decide whether descriptor parsing/derivation stays in Python or uses a helper/library seam backed by Rust tooling such as rust-miniscript or BDK
Decide the exact v1 descriptor input format and whether both external and change descriptors are mandatory for multisig verification
Confirm the initial Electrum protocol compatibility target and transport assumptions for local household deployments
Decide whether v1 will persist only verification results or also permit opt-in persistence of descriptor sources
Determine whether a remembered source should store raw descriptor material, encrypted descriptor material, or only an indirect Sparrow/local-file reference
Research Sparrow wallet-file encryption and unlock flow from primary sources before promising native wallet-file support
Define the exact claim language for verified, stale, failed, and partial-coverage states so the UI does not over-promise
openQuestions: Is there a production-credible Python-native descriptor parsing and derivation stack for the descriptor types we care about, or should the project plan on a Rust-backed helper from the outset?
Should v1 verification be balance-only, or should it also query history/UTXOs to better explain drift when the balance mismatches?
What is the minimum safe scan policy for descriptor-derived addresses or scriptPubKeys: fixed gap limit, wallet-provided range, or operator override?
If persisted sources are allowed, what encryption-at-rest posture is acceptable for stored descriptor material in a single-operator private app?
Can Sparrow wallet-file decryption be supported safely and maintainably enough to include in Feature-23 proper, or should it remain a follow-on story after manual descriptor sessions ship?
